title: Push-driven channel wake in the existing terminal session
purpose: Implement the existing TUI consumer of the single channel session owner described in NCH-001 R4a and norn-channels/design.json. The user prioritized a real idle wake into the current interactive Norn session before workspace redesign. This brief owns only the terminal consumer and its public-path regression evidence; root construction, CLI flags, live MCP activation and durable delivery are separate coordinated walls.
task: Wire one push-driven idle wake arm and run the established external-message turn lifecycle. Keep channel content as typed persisted external input, preserve the draft composer and root cancellation semantics, and test the real run_app path through a Rust stdio source and pseudo-terminal. Parent owns all Rust builds, venue checks, review and landing.

requirements.title: Idle wake without polling or operator-prompt conversion
requirements.spec: WHEN the installed session owner reports published Wake input while the TUI is idle, the terminal event loop SHALL wake through a dedicated push future and start the ordinary external-message turn path without creating or slash-parsing a user prompt. The session owner SHALL perform framed persistence and retained quota release. Hold and NextTurn input alone SHALL NOT wake this idle path. The existing turn-local cancellation, rendering, follow-up prompts and pending child results SHALL remain available. A closed or failed wake owner SHALL return a named typed TUI error rather than spinning or silently falling back. WHEN a channel-triggered turn is interrupted, fails, or stops before completion, the TUI SHALL pause automatic channel wake, preserve retained input and display the reason. The next ordinary operator turn SHALL rearm automatic channel wake; an operator follow-up submitted during that channel turn also rearms it. This state SHALL belong to the TUI event loop and SHALL NOT create a retry timer or drop the inbox.
acceptance: The channel wake select arm is separate from the RENDER_TICK arm. A session without channels waits without a new timer or task.
The turn starts from a typed channel wake seed; its first request and event history contain the escaped source frame exactly once, with no fabricated empty UserMessage.
An external payload beginning with /model or /quit remains external content and does not dispatch a host command.
Existing composer text is preserved while the idle channel turn runs. Follow-up handling, root cancellation ownership and ordinary turns reuse the established run_turn lifecycle.
Hold and NextTurn retain their existing owner policy: only Wake makes the idle readiness future resolve.

A distinct typed McpChannelDeliveryEvent emitted after persistence renders source and raw external content as an external-channel transcript row, preserving the existing composer. Rendering neutralizes terminal control sequences; the event refers to the exact persisted framed UserMessage and never pretends to be operator keystrokes or an agent sender.

A channel wake rejected before persistence does not auto-loop. The terminal stays interactive, retained input remains charged, the pause reason is visible, and a new ordinary operator turn can persist that input exactly once and rearm later autonomous Wake input. Ctrl+C retains its existing turn-local cancellation token.

requirements.title: Real terminal session and Rust MCP push regression
requirements.spec: A protocol-clean Rust custom test harness SHALL launch itself as both a stdio MCP fixture and a real run_app process in a pseudo-terminal. Test synchronization SHALL use protocol messages and an owned loopback connection, never filesystem or render-timer polling. The fixture SHALL prove a push arriving after the interactive UI is idle causes a provider call and exact persisted channel event. Test deadlines are hang diagnostics only.
acceptance: An ordinary cargo test workspace run executes named real-TUI channel scenarios and returns nonzero on failure. MCP subprocess mode writes only JSON-RPC data to stdout.
The parent waits for the actual terminal input panel, then commands the Rust source to emit; provider capture proves that push initiates the request without typing Enter.
A channel payload resembling a slash command reaches the provider as an escaped frame and preserves model/session identity and any existing composer draft.

Held input remains retained and absent from an ordinary provider request; NextTurn input joins an independently submitted prompt. The fixture records retained accounting and provider message history. Explicit Hold release/deny remains covered by NCH-001 R3 receiver fixtures.
Rust build and execution evidence comes only from parent-dispatched 205 verification.

The real-TUI replay-refusal specimen fails once before consumption, proves zero provider calls and one retained message while paused, retries through an ordinary typed prompt with exactly one original channel event, then accepts a later autonomous wake without another Enter key.

boundaries: No new TuiInputs fields, daemon, PTY transport for agent state, workspace redesign or numeric production limits.
No source is enabled by metadata and no notification provides tool approval or system authority.
event_loop.rs also differs in the independent model candidate; parent integrates that overlap after its commit, preserving both changes.
These scenarios do not stand in for full Cambium/Hammerbarn adapter proof, independent review or a venue exact-commit battery.
verification: Rustfmt and source review locally only. Parent serializes Rust tests and strict Clippy on 205.
